summary: Tooltips in the window show the keyboard shortcut of what their button does, and on macOS the window's own menus and its tooltips show Finder's keys. Kit Buttons use `tooltip_with_action(label, &Action, Some(FINDER))`: Back, Forward, the four view buttons (`view_button` takes the action), Show Sidebar, Hide Sidebar, the Nushell panel's close button and the filter bar's close button. Controls that are plain divs use a new helper, `shortcut_tooltip(label, &Action)` in src/finder/toolbar.rs (pub(super)), which builds the kit's Tooltip from an observed element `shortcut-tip` and gives it the action: the scope bar's funnel and (i), the tab bar's + (which had no tooltip) and the × of the tab that shows, and the sidebar's Settings gear. The other tabs' × keep the plain "Close Tab". In src/actions.rs the key table moved into `key_table(mac, cx)`, and `bind_keys` passes `cfg!(target_os = "macos")`. Finder's key is bound first for Back, Forward, Enclosing Folder and Move to Trash (`secondary-up` now comes before `alt-up`), and when `mac` is true those keys are bound once more at the end of the table, before the `--term` aliases are derived. The macOS menu bar shows an action's first binding and the kit's menus and tooltips its last one, so a Mac shows Finder's key in both, and Linux and Windows keep Alt+Left, Alt+Right, Alt+Up and Delete.
changelog: Tooltips show the keyboard shortcut of what their button does: Back, Forward, the four view buttons, Show Sidebar and Hide Sidebar, Filter with Nushell and Search Syntax in the scope bar, the close buttons of the filter bar and the Nushell panel, and the sidebar's Settings button. The tab bar's + has a tooltip, New Tab, and the × of the tab that is showing names Cmd+W. Back, Forward, Enclosing Folder, and Move to Trash have Finder's shortcut and the one Explorer and the Linux file managers use; menus and tooltips show Finder's on macOS and the other on Linux and Windows. On macOS that corrects the item menu and the Actions menu, which showed a bare ⌫ for Move to Trash instead of Cmd+Backspace, and Go › Enclosing Folder in the menu bar, which showed Alt+Up instead of Cmd+Up.
behaviour_changes: Linux (seen in pictures; Windows has the same keys): a tooltip shows the key after the name, in the muted colour. Back Alt+Left, Forward Alt+Right, as Icons / as List / as Columns / as Gallery Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+4, Show Sidebar and Hide Sidebar Ctrl+Alt+S, Filter with Nushell Ctrl+Alt+F, Search Syntax Ctrl+/, Settings (the sidebar's gear) Ctrl+, and Remove the filter (the filter bar's ×) Ctrl+Alt+F.
The tab bar's + has a tooltip where it had none: New Tab Ctrl+T.
The × of the tab that shows reads Close Tab Ctrl+W. The × of the other tabs still reads Close Tab, because the keys close the tab that shows.
The Nushell panel's close button reads Close with the key drawn as Ctrl+` instead of the text "Close (Ctrl-`)".

These tooltips are wider. Near the window's right edge they open to the left of the pointer (the scope bar's, seen at 1100 and at 760 points wide) or above the button (the two close buttons), and stay inside the window.
A disabled Back or Forward button still shows its tooltip, now with the key, as it showed the name before.

No visible change in menus on Linux or Windows: Move to Trash still shows Delete. The key the window would show for Enclosing Folder is now Alt+Up instead of Ctrl+Up, but no menu or tooltip shows that command.
Every key does what it did. Checked for the keys that are bound in a new order or twice: Ctrl+[ and ], Alt+Left and Right, Ctrl+Up, Alt+Up, Ctrl+Backspace and Delete.

macOS, from the code and from binding the Mac's table on Linux, not run on a Mac: the Back and Forward tooltips show Cmd+[ and Cmd+] (without the second binding they would show Alt+Left and Alt+Right).
macOS, same basis: Move to Trash in the item menu and in the Actions menu shows Cmd+Backspace instead of a bare ⌫.

macOS, same basis: Go › Enclosing Folder in the menu bar shows Cmd+Up instead of Alt+Up, and Cmd+Up is its key equivalent. Go › Back and Forward and File › Move to Trash already showed Cmd+[, Cmd+] and Cmd+Backspace and still do.
In `--term` the Ctrl aliases are still bound last, so tooltips show the Ctrl form there, as menus do.

docs/manual.md: a paragraph in "The window" on what button tooltips show and which buttons name their keys; a paragraph at the top of "Keyboard shortcuts" on the four commands with two shortcuts and which one menus and tooltips show; "Menus and tooltips show the Ctrl form" in the terminal section; and in "Filters and Smart Folders", that Cmd+Alt+F removes the filter as the close button does.

`--do hover:<id>` works in examples/screenshot.rs (so in shot.sh) and `hover:<id>` in examples/drive.rs. A hover rests the mouse on an element by ID; in the screenshot example the tooltip is up when the picture is taken.
left_out: Nothing was run on macOS or Windows. The macOS half rests on gpui-pre-macos 0.3.10 (`create_menu_item` takes `bindings_for_action(..).find_or_first(..)` against Zed's own contexts, which fffinder's never match, so the first binding), on the kit (`Kbd::binding_for_action` and the menus take `highest_precedence_binding_for_action*`, the last binding that isn't shadowed; kbd.rs draws `delete` as ⌫ on macOS), and on two runs on Linux with `key_table(true, cx)` forced in `bind_keys`. See the notes for what those runs showed.

No test asserts the key drawn inside a tooltip. The kit draws it as plain text with no ID and no debug selector, for its Buttons and for `Tooltip::action` alike. Tests cover the lookup the tooltip makes (`Kbd::binding_for_action(action, Some(FINDER), window)`) and, for the div-based ones, that the tooltip appears with its label. A wrong action passed to `tooltip_with_action` or `shortcut_tooltip` would only show in a picture.
The smoke hovers over `back` and `view-list` from the plan are not included: a kit Button's tooltip shows nothing to the harness, so they could assert nothing.

Close Tab names Cmd+W on the showing tab even while the keyboard is in the split pane, where Cmd+W closes the split pane first. Every toolbar tooltip of a pane without the keyboard has the same limit. Left for split-active-pane.

By the first-binding rule the macOS menu bar shows F5 for View › Refresh, Return for File › Open and Space for File › Quick Look. The verifier put Refresh outside this brief and the other two are the same case; see "Found, not fixed".
The folder tree's Move to Trash is bound twice on a Mac too, and no test presses it with the keys bound twice. It goes through the same dispatch as the four that are pressed.

`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: src/term is untouched and calls nothing that changed (grepped for bind_keys, key_table, shortcut_tooltip and actions:: in src/term, src/macos.rs, src/win.rs and src/main.rs).
Steps still can't name numbered IDs such as ("close-tab", 1). The implementer's two Close Tab pictures were taken with a temporary `hover:close-tab#1` that is not committed.
CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.

review_fixes: Added tests/finder.rs a_key_bound_twice_acts_once. The repeated macOS bindings are safe only while the handlers of Back, Forward, Enclosing Folder and Move to Trash don't call cx.propagate(), and nothing checked that: the existing Back test starts one folder deep, so a second step back has nowhere to go. The test binds the whole key table a second time through fffinder::actions::bind_keys and presses the four keys from two folders deep. With cx.propagate() added to go_back it fails with two steps back, and with it added to move_to_trash it fails on the notification of the second trash.

The filter bar's close button ("Remove the filter") now names Cmd+Alt+F with tooltip_with_action(.., &ToggleFilter, Some(FINDER)). The implementer's report called the Settings gear the one remaining tooltip whose command has a key; this was another, and toggle_filter with the bar open is exactly close_filter. Added tests/controls.rs the_keys_on_the_filter_bars_close_button_remove_the_filter, since no test pressed the keys with the bar open, and one sentence to the manual's "Filters and Smart Folders".

It now begins "A button's tooltip says what the button does." The list of buttons that name their keys gained the filter bar's close button.

Commit message: the filter bar's close button in the body and in the Changelog paragraph, the new test, and what binding the Mac's table on Linux showed.

notes:
CHECK ONCE ON A MAC (nothing here could run there): the Go menu shows Cmd+[, Cmd+] and Cmd+Up; File › Move to Trash shows Cmd+Backspace; Move to Trash in the item menu and in the Actions menu shows Cmd+Backspace; the Back tooltip shows Cmd+[; and one press of Cmd+[ goes back one folder. macOS CI runs two tests with Mac-only expectations: the_keys_shown_for_going_back_forward_and_up_are_this_systems (cmd-[, cmd-], cmd-up) and the_item_menu_shows_this_systems_keys_for_move_to_trash (kbd:cmd-backspace drawn, kbd:delete not). If the reading of the kit is wrong, CI fails there.

What the Linux runs with the Mac's table showed (`key_table(true, cx)` forced in bind_keys, not committed): tests/basics.rs, columns.rs, file_ops.rs, finder.rs and folder_tree.rs passed (apart from the known root-only failure), so every key acted once and as before; in tests/controls.rs only the two tests above failed, with ctrl-[ shown for Back and no kbd:delete in the item menu; and with their macOS expectations spelled with Ctrl for Cmd, those two passed.

For briefs still to come:
- history-menus: Back and Forward are `pill_button(..).tooltip_with_action("Back", &GoBack, Some(FINDER))` and the same for Forward. Keep the action if the label changes or the button gets a menu or a wrapper, or the key disappears from the tooltip. A kit Button's tooltip shows nothing to the test harness.
- show-in-enclosing-folder-key, type-select-space, smart-folder-save-and-leaks, split-active-pane (all add to src/actions.rs): the bindings are now the `vec![..]` in `key_table(mac, cx)`, not an array in `bind_keys`. Where an action gets a second key, the order decides what is shown: the macOS menu bar shows the first one bound, and the window's own menus and tooltips the last. If Finder's key should show on a Mac and another key elsewhere, bind Finder's first and add it to the `if mac` block at the end, and add the action to TWO_KEY_ACTIONS in the unit tests, which pin the exact order. A handler whose key is bound twice must not call `cx.propagate()` after acting; tests/finder.rs a_key_bound_twice_acts_once presses Back, Forward, Enclosing Folder and Move to Trash that way.
- split-active-pane: the × of the showing tab names CloseWindow's keys (Cmd+W) whichever pane has the keyboard, though in the split pane Cmd+W closes that pane first (`close_tab_or_window` in src/finder/tab_bar.rs). With an active pane to ask, the tooltip could drop the keys while the split pane is the active one.
- tab-bar-overflow, tab-drop-and-close, restore-session-tabs (src/finder/tab_bar.rs): `new-tab` and the showing tab's `("close-tab", ix)` now have tooltips built by `shortcut_tooltip`; the other tabs' × use the plain `Tooltip::new("Close Tab")`. tests/controls.rs tab_bar_tooltips_name_their_shortcuts hovers `new-tab`, `("close-tab", 1)` and `("close-tab", 0)` after Cmd+T in a window opened with `workspace: true`, so keep those IDs, or change the test with them. A new way to close a tab (middle-click, Close Other Tabs) has no key, so it needs no key in a tooltip.
- smart-folder-save-and-leaks, recent-searches, regex-content-search (src/finder/bars.rs, filter.rs, toolbar.rs): a new icon button whose command has a key should name it. For a kit Button use `.tooltip_with_action(label, &Action, Some(FINDER))`; for a div use `super::toolbar::shortcut_tooltip(label, &Action)`, which tests find as the element `shortcut-tip` with the label as its `label()`. The scope bar's `filter-toggle` and `search-help` and the filter bar's `close-filter` already do. The manual lists the buttons that name their keys in "The window"; add to that list.
- context-menus-fit: tests/controls.rs the_item_menu_shows_this_systems_keys_for_move_to_trash right-clicks a file in an ordinary folder in the list view and looks for the kit's selector of the key drawn beside Move to Trash (`kbd:delete`, or `kbd:cmd-backspace` on macOS). If the item menu's Move to Trash is renamed or left out in some places, keep the item and its action in an ordinary folder, or change the test with it.
- split-view-toolbar-clip (src/finder/toolbar.rs, sidebar.rs): only the tooltip calls changed on `back`, `forward`, the `view_button` closure (it takes the action as a fifth argument), `show-sidebar` and `hide-sidebar`. No width or layout changed.
- preview-page-keys: its handlers call `cx.propagate()` (`preview_key` in src/finder/pdf.rs). That is fine for them, because they propagate only when they did nothing. Don't copy the pattern to an action that is bound twice and has acted.
- Anyone taking pictures: shot.sh now takes `--do hover:<element id>` and the tooltip is in the picture. IDs that are a name and a number can't be given.

Found, not fixed:
- macOS menu bar, from reading the code, not run on a Mac: it shows an action's first binding, so View › Refresh shows F5 (bound before Cmd+R), File › Open shows Return (before Cmd+Down and Cmd+O) and File › Quick Look shows Space (before Cmd+Y). Finder shows Cmd+O and Cmd+Y. Those are also the menu items' key equivalents. Binding the Cmd key first for each, as this change does for the four, would fix what is shown; the keys themselves all stay bound.
- On a Mac the kit's text fields take Alt+Left, Alt+Right and Cmd+Up for moving the caret (gpui-base input/base/state.rs), so while the search field has the keyboard those three don't go back, forward or up. Cmd+[ and Cmd+] do: a one-line field doesn't handle the kit's Outdent and Indent, so the keys fall through to the window. On Linux every key a tooltip names works from the search field (tried in review: Ctrl+[, Ctrl+], Alt+Left, Alt+Right, Ctrl+2, Ctrl+Alt+S, Ctrl+`, Ctrl+Alt+F, Ctrl+/ and Ctrl+,). The manual's "Both work on every system" is true of the file views, as its shortcut tables are.
